```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

model_names <- trimws(strsplit(params$models, ",")[[1]])
thresholds  <- as.numeric(trimws(strsplit(params$review_thresholds, ",")[[1]]))
severe_cut  <- params$severe_cut
```

## What this reports

The pipeline writes one CSV per cross-validation fold, each containing the rows
it was given with `training` / `validation` flags and a
`predicted_qu_motion_score` column. Concatenating the `validation == 1` rows
across the five folds gives one out-of-fold prediction per scan: every
prediction comes from a model that never saw that subject.

Three things are reported that a plain correlation does not show.

1. **A mean-predictor baseline.** `std_rmse` is error divided by label SD, so a
   model that always predicts the mean scores exactly 1.0. Values at or above
   1.0 mean nothing useful was learned, however small the p-value.
2. **Between- versus within-scanner signal.** If scanner identity shifts the
   label mean, a model that learns only that offset earns a pooled correlation
   while carrying no within-group signal.
3. **Screening performance.** Correlation is the wrong metric for a QC filter.
   What matters is how many scans must be reviewed to catch the bad ones, which
   is insensitive to the range compression that depresses `r`.

```{r load}
read_model <- function(name) {
  dir   <- file.path(params$project_dir, "doc", "models", name)
  files <- list.files(dir, pattern = paste0("^", name, "_fold_\\d+\\.csv$"),
                      full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) {
    message("no fold CSVs found for ", name, " in ", dir, " -- skipping")
    return(NULL)
  }
  map_dfr(files, function(f) {
    read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
      filter(validation == 1) %>%
      mutate(fold  = as.integer(sub(".*_fold_(\\d+)\\.csv$", "\\1", f)),
             model = name)
  })
}

oof <- map(model_names, read_model) %>% compact()
stopifnot("none of the requested models had fold CSVs" = length(oof) > 0)
names(oof) <- map_chr(oof, ~ .x$model[1])

is_frame_level <- map_lgl(oof, ~ "frame_index" %in% names(.x) &&
                               any(!is.na(.x$frame_index)))

# collapse frame rows to one prediction per scan so every model is on the
# same units regardless of whether it was trained per frame
per_scan <- function(d) {
  if (!("frame_index" %in% names(d))) return(d)
  d %>%
    group_by(model, fold, scan) %>%
    summarise(
      subject_id           = first(subject_id),
      session_id           = first(session_id),
      run_id               = first(run_id),
      dir                  = first(dir),
      scanner_manufacturer = first(scanner_manufacturer),
      QU_motion            = mean(QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE),
      predicted_qu_motion_score = mean(predicted_qu_motion_score, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_frames             = dplyr::n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
scan_level <- map(oof, per_scan)
```

```{r populations}
# Models evaluated on different sets of scans are answering different
# questions and must not share a comparison table. A model trained on an
# artifact-enriched subset faces a base rate several times the cohort's, so its
# correlation is not on the same scale as a cohort model's. Group by the actual
# set of scans each model was scored on.
scan_sets <- map(scan_level, ~ sort(unique(.x$scan)))
reps <- list(); pop_id <- integer(length(scan_sets))
for (i in seq_along(scan_sets)) {
  hit <- 0L
  for (j in seq_along(reps)) if (identical(scan_sets[[i]], reps[[j]])) { hit <- j; break }
  if (hit == 0L) { reps[[length(reps) + 1L]] <- scan_sets[[i]]; hit <- length(reps) }
  pop_id[i] <- hit
}

pop_label <- map_chr(seq_along(scan_level), function(i) {
  d <- scan_level[[i]]
  sprintf("P%d (%d scans, label mean %.3f)", pop_id[i], nrow(d),
          mean(d$QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE))
})
names(pop_id) <- names(pop_label) <- names(scan_level)

info <- tibble(
  model      = names(scan_level),
  population = pop_label,
  level      = ifelse(is_frame_level, "per frame", "per scan"),
  scans      = map_int(scan_level, nrow),
  subjects   = map_int(scan_level, ~ n_distinct(.x$subject_id)),
  label_mean = map_dbl(scan_level, ~ mean(.x$QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE)),
  label_sd   = map_dbl(scan_level, ~ sd(.x$QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE)),
  pct_zero   = map_dbl(scan_level, ~ mean(.x$QU_motion == 0, na.rm = TRUE))
)
kable(info, digits = 4, caption = "Out-of-fold data loaded, grouped by evaluation population")

n_pop <- length(unique(pop_id))
```

```{r popwarn, results='asis'}
if (n_pop > 1) {
  cat("::: {.callout-important}\n",
      "**", n_pop, " different evaluation populations are loaded.** Metrics are ",
      "only comparable within a population. A model scored on an ",
      "artifact-enriched subset sees a higher base rate than one scored on the ",
      "full cohort, so a lower `r` there does not mean a worse model. Tables ",
      "below carry a `population` column; compare only within it.\n:::\n",
      sep = "")
}
```

```{r helpers}
# Rank-based AUC: the Mann-Whitney statistic. Handles ties, no pROC dependency.
auc <- function(score, positive) {
  ok <- !is.na(score) & !is.na(positive)
  score <- score[ok]; positive <- as.integer(positive[ok])
  n1 <- sum(positive == 1); n0 <- sum(positive == 0)
  if (n1 == 0 || n0 == 0) return(NA_real_)
  r <- rank(score)
  (sum(r[positive == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

metrics <- function(truth, pred) {
  ok <- !is.na(truth) & !is.na(pred)
  truth <- truth[ok]; pred <- pred[ok]
  if (length(truth) < 3 || sd(truth) == 0 || sd(pred) == 0) {
    return(tibble(n = length(truth), r = NA_real_, spearman = NA_real_,
                  rmse = NA_real_, label_sd = NA_real_, std_rmse = NA_real_,
                  bias = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_, intercept = NA_real_))
  }
  sd_t <- sd(truth)
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((pred - truth)^2))
  fit  <- stats::lm(pred ~ truth)
  tibble(n = length(truth),
         r         = stats::cor(truth, pred),
         spearman  = stats::cor(truth, pred, method = "spearman"),
         rmse      = rmse,
         label_sd  = sd_t,
         std_rmse  = rmse / sd_t,
         bias      = mean(pred - truth),
         slope     = unname(stats::coef(fit)[2]),
         intercept = unname(stats::coef(fit)[1]))
}

# attach the population label to any per-model table
with_pop <- function(tb) {
  tb %>% mutate(population = pop_label[model], .after = model)
}
```

## Headline metrics

```{r headline}
map_dfr(scan_level, ~ metrics(.x$QU_motion, .x$predicted_qu_motion_score),
        .id = "model") %>%
  with_pop() %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Pooled out-of-fold performance, per scan")
```

`std_rmse` below 1.0 means the model beats predicting the mean of its own
population. `slope` below 1.0 is range compression: the model pulls clean scans
up and bad scans down toward the middle, which depresses `r` without
necessarily harming its usefulness as a screen.

### Per fold

```{r perfold}
map_dfr(scan_level, function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(fold) %>%
    group_modify(~ metrics(.x$QU_motion, .x$predicted_qu_motion_score)) %>%
    ungroup()
}, .id = "model") %>%
  with_pop() %>%
  select(model, population, fold, n, r, spearman, rmse, label_sd, std_rmse) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Per-fold metrics")
```

Spread across folds is the honest error bar on the pooled figure. Where folds
hold only a few dozen scans the per-fold `r` carries a confidence interval of
roughly ±0.3 or wider, so read the pooled row and treat the per-fold column as
a consistency check rather than five independent estimates.

## Scanner confound

A model that learns only which scanner produced an image earns a pooled
correlation while carrying no within-scanner signal.

```{r confound}
confound <- function(d) {
  tot <- var(d$QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE)
  grp <- d %>% group_by(scanner_manufacturer) %>%
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(), gm = mean(QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  overall <- mean(d$QU_motion, na.rm = TRUE)
  eta2 <- if (is.na(tot) || tot == 0) NA_real_ else
    sum(grp$n * (grp$gm - overall)^2) / ((nrow(d) - 1) * tot)

  within <- d %>% group_by(scanner_manufacturer) %>%
    filter(dplyr::n() > 2, sd(QU_motion) > 0, sd(predicted_qu_motion_score) > 0) %>%
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
              label_mean = mean(QU_motion),
              pred_mean  = mean(predicted_qu_motion_score),
              within_r   = stats::cor(QU_motion, predicted_qu_motion_score),
              .groups = "drop")

  list(table = within,
       summary = tibble(
         pooled_r       = stats::cor(d$QU_motion, d$predicted_qu_motion_score),
         within_r       = if (nrow(within) == 0) NA_real_ else
                            sum(within$within_r * within$n) / sum(within$n),
         scanner_eta2   = eta2,
         scanner_only_r = sqrt(pmax(eta2, 0))))
}

cf <- map(scan_level, confound)
map_dfr(cf, "table", .id = "model") %>% with_pop() %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Within-scanner performance")
map_dfr(cf, "summary", .id = "model") %>% with_pop() %>%
  kable(digits = 4,
        caption = "Pooled vs within-scanner. scanner_only_r is what a group-mean lookup table would score.")
```

::: {.callout-important}
If `pooled_r` is much larger than `within_r`, the model is reading the scanner
rather than the image. If `pooled_r` is below `scanner_only_r`, it performs
worse than a lookup table keyed on manufacturer.
:::

## Screening performance

How much of the cohort must a human review, and what fraction of bad scans does
that catch. AUC is threshold-free and insensitive to range compression.

```{r aucs}
screen <- function(d) {
  p <- d$predicted_qu_motion_score
  map_dfr(list(
    list(lab = "any artifact", tgt = d$QU_motion > 0),
    list(lab = paste0("severe (>=", severe_cut, ")"), tgt = d$QU_motion >= severe_cut)
  ), function(s) tibble(target = s$lab,
                        prevalence = mean(s$tgt, na.rm = TRUE),
                        AUC = auc(p, s$tgt)))
}
map_dfr(scan_level, screen, .id = "model") %>% with_pop() %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Discrimination (threshold-free)")
```

```{r thresholds}
threshold_table <- function(d) {
  p <- d$predicted_qu_motion_score
  targets <- list(d$QU_motion > 0, d$QU_motion >= severe_cut)
  names(targets) <- c("any artifact", paste0("severe (>=", severe_cut, ")"))
  map_dfr(names(targets), function(tname) {
    tgt <- targets[[tname]]
    map_dfr(thresholds, function(k) {
      flag <- p >= k
      tp <- sum(flag & tgt, na.rm = TRUE)
      fp <- sum(flag & !tgt, na.rm = TRUE)
      fn <- sum(!flag & tgt, na.rm = TRUE)
      tibble(target = tname, threshold = k,
             flagged     = mean(flag, na.rm = TRUE),
             n_flagged   = sum(flag, na.rm = TRUE),
             sensitivity = if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else NA_real_,
             precision   = if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else NA_real_,
             missed      = fn)
    })
  })
}
map_dfr(scan_level, threshold_table, .id = "model") %>% with_pop() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        caption = "Review burden against catch rate. `flagged` is the share of that population a human would review.")
```

```{r roc, fig.height=4.5}
# Vectorised sweep: sort once by descending score; running counts of positives
# and negatives give every point on the curve.
roc_points <- function(score, positive) {
  ok <- !is.na(score) & !is.na(positive)
  score <- score[ok]; positive <- as.integer(positive[ok])
  if (sum(positive) == 0 || sum(1 - positive) == 0) return(NULL)
  pos <- positive[order(score, decreasing = TRUE)]
  tibble(tpr = c(0, cumsum(pos)) / sum(pos),
         fpr = c(0, cumsum(1 - pos)) / sum(1 - pos))
}
map_dfr(scan_level, function(d) {
  p <- d$predicted_qu_motion_score
  bind_rows(
    roc_points(p, d$QU_motion > 0) %>% mutate(target = "any artifact"),
    roc_points(p, d$QU_motion >= severe_cut) %>%
      mutate(target = paste0("severe (>=", severe_cut, ")"))
  ) %>% mutate(model = d$model[1])
}) %>%
  mutate(series = paste0(model, " — ", pop_label[model])) %>%
  ggplot(aes(fpr, tpr, colour = series)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ target) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical") +
  labs(x = "False positive rate", y = "True positive rate", colour = NULL,
       title = "ROC")
```

## Error by severity

Pooled error is dominated by whichever rating is most common. Breaking it down
shows where the model actually fails.

```{r bysev}
map_dfr(scan_level, function(d) {
  bind_rows(
    d %>% mutate(stratum = "all"),
    d %>% filter(QU_motion == 0) %>% mutate(stratum = "clean (0)"),
    d %>% filter(QU_motion > 0) %>% mutate(stratum = "any artifact (>0)"),
    d %>% filter(QU_motion >= severe_cut) %>%
      mutate(stratum = paste0("severe (>=", severe_cut, ")"))
  ) %>%
    group_by(stratum) %>%
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
              rmse = sqrt(mean((predicted_qu_motion_score - QU_motion)^2)),
              bias = mean(predicted_qu_motion_score - QU_motion),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(model = d$model[1])
}) %>%
  with_pop() %>%
  select(model, population, stratum, n, rmse, bias) %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        caption = "Error by severity. Negative bias on severe scans means the model under-calls them.")
```

## Per-frame behaviour

```{r perframe}
frame_models <- names(oof)[is_frame_level]

frame_gaps <- function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(scan) %>% filter(dplyr::n() == 2) %>%
    summarise(label_gap = abs(diff(QU_motion)),
              pred_gap  = abs(diff(predicted_qu_motion_score)),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(model = d$model[1])
}

if (length(frame_models) == 0) {
  cat("No frame-level model loaded; nothing to report here.\n")
} else {
  map_dfr(oof[frame_models], frame_gaps) %>%
    group_by(model) %>%
    summarise(scans          = dplyr::n(),
              labels_differ  = mean(label_gap > 0),
              mean_label_gap = mean(label_gap),
              mean_pred_gap  = mean(pred_gap),
              r_gap          = if (sd(label_gap) > 0 && sd(pred_gap) > 0)
                                 stats::cor(label_gap, pred_gap) else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    with_pop() %>%
    kable(digits = 4,
          caption = "Agreement between the two volumes of a scan. `r_gap` asks whether the model reproduces the rater's volume-to-volume differences.")
}
```

```{r perframe_plot, fig.height=4}
if (length(frame_models) > 0) {
  g <- map_dfr(oof[frame_models], frame_gaps) %>% filter(label_gap > 0)
  if (nrow(g) > 0) {
    print(
      g %>%
        mutate(panel = paste0(model, "\n", pop_label[model])) %>%
        ggplot(aes(label_gap, pred_gap)) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.05, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.9) +
        geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
        facet_wrap(~ panel) +
        labs(x = "Rater difference between volumes",
             y = "Model difference between volumes",
             title = "Does the model see what the rater saw between volumes?",
             subtitle = "Only scans whose two volumes were rated differently")
    )
  }
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
`r_gap` is the question the split-frames architecture exists to answer. Near
zero means the model gives both volumes of a scan nearly the same score however
the rater scored them, so per-volume labels bought nothing. A model whose
training labels duplicated one file-level score across both volumes cannot
score well here — it was never shown a reason to separate them.
:::

## Model comparison

```{r compare, results='asis'}
base <- map_dfr(scan_level, ~ metrics(.x$QU_motion, .x$predicted_qu_motion_score),
                .id = "model") %>%
  left_join(map_dfr(scan_level, function(d) {
    tibble(model = d$model[1],
           auc_any    = auc(d$predicted_qu_motion_score, d$QU_motion > 0),
           auc_severe = auc(d$predicted_qu_motion_score, d$QU_motion >= severe_cut))
  }), by = "model") %>%
  mutate(population = pop_label[model])

for (p in unique(base$population)) {
  sub <- base %>% filter(population == p) %>%
    select(model, n, r, spearman, std_rmse, slope, bias, auc_any, auc_severe)
  cat("\n\n### ", p, "\n\n", sep = "")
  if (nrow(sub) == 1) {
    cat("Only one model on this population, so there is nothing to compare it ",
        "against here.\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  # cat() rather than print(): inside results='asis' this emits the markdown
  # table directly instead of a console-formatted representation of it
  cat(kable(sub, digits = 4), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Two cautions on any comparison above.

Models trained on different label sets are scored against different targets. In
particular, a model trained on labels corrected only where an earlier model
erred will look better on exactly those cases, because the correction and the
evaluation share a selection rule.

Models in different populations are not compared at all. An artifact-enriched
subset has a base rate several times the cohort's; `r` computed there answers a
different question and is not interchangeable with the cohort figure.
:::
